cards.group: The kingdom as a world

readings.label: His sentence
readings.original: The original of the figurative language of the Prophets is the comparison of a kingdom to the frame of heaven and earth, and the parts of the one to the like parts of the other.
readings.modern: The prophets' picture-language starts from one comparison. A kingdom is like the whole frame of heaven and earth, and each part of the kingdom answers to the matching part of that frame.

proof.original: 1. The comparison of a Kingdom to the world may appear out of Isay 51.16, where the new founding of the political world or kingdom of the Iews is exprest by planting the heavens and laying the foundations of the earth. I have put my words in thy mouth and have covered thee in the shaddow of mine hand that I may plant the heavens and lay the foundations of the earth, and say unto Zion, Thou art my people. See the Chalde Paraphrast. And in the same sence is heaven and earth to be taken in Isa:1.2. Hagg:2.21. and c. And so in the Apocalyps, Rejoyce the heavens and ye that dwell in them. Wo to the inhabiters of the earth and sea

proof.original: 2. The signification of the Sun moon and stars is manifested by these instances. When Ioseph dreamed that the Sun moon and eleven stars should do obeisance to him, Iacob interprets it of himself his wife and sons, comparing his family to the Vnivers as if it were a little kingdom Gen. 37. ‡ Sextus Empirius saith that the Egyptians – – – ‡ Sextus Empirius saith that the Egyptians assimilate the Sun to the King and to the right eye and the moon to the Queen and to the left eye and the five Planets to Lictors or staff-bearers and the fixt stars to the rest of the people. Sex. Empir. adv. mathem. l. 5. p 114. e. The horn cast down of the host of heaven and of the stars to the grownd. Yea he magnified himself even to the Prince of the host. Dan 8.10. being the stars are put for the saints, the chief men of the church so in the Apocalyps the seven stars are the Angels of the Church that is their Bishops. In which sense the Moon also may respect the Church as the Sun doth the Kingdom. For in the Kingdom of Christ, the Church is the Queen, being the wife of the Lamb Apoc 19. And therefore the new moons were celebrated by the Iews as a type of the future renovation of the Church. And when the church is in a Christian Kingdom, the Priests of any religion may be in the Kingdom. * * For so in Apoc 12 where the Woman in heaven (who is the church) tramples upon the Moon it seems to be with respect to religion. The Eastern nations taught that the Sun. – – – – morning star. the eastern nations that the Sun – – – – The Sun immutably represents the king, the Moon the next in power to the king [suppose the Pontifex maximus with his mystical body of Priests the Planet Venus the Queen, the rest of the greater stars the great men of the kingdom. Achmet. Chap. 16, ex Ind. Pers. and Ægypt. Yet Lucifer which is the same with Venus does sometimes signify a king, as in Isa 14.12, where the king of Babylon is called by this name: suppose in respect of God or Christ the King of kings, or perhaps in respect of the king of the Medes whom some describe a greater king then that of Babylon. And so Christ is called the morning star. Here Christ being the Prince or Sun of righteousness (as he is called in Mal. 4.2) the stars are put for the Saints.

proof.original: 3. Thou hast said in thine heart I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my Throne above the stars of God, I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation in the sides of the North. I will ascend above the heights of the clouds, and c. This is spoken of the king of Babylon exalting himself above all Kings and earthly dominions. Isa 14.13. Thy greatnes [O Nebuchadnezzar is grown and reacheth unto the heaven Dan. 4.22. And thou Capernaum which art exalted unto heaven Mat. 11.23. By all which it may appear that heaven signifies any high and exalted estate, and earth a low one.

proof.original: 6. Hurt not the earth nor the sea, Rev 7.3. that is the two sorts of people signified by the earth and the sea as is expounded in chap. 12.12. Those that slay with the sword shall be assembled from all sides: Kings of nations and their armies shall come to spoile. Ier 12.9. The burden of the Beasts of the South i.e. the bands of Egypt. Isa. 30.6. I have given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar King of Babylon my servant, and the beasts of the field have I given him also to serve him, and all nations shal serve him. Ier. 27.6. and 28.14. I will also send wild beasts among you which shall rob you of your children and destroy your cattel and make you few in number, and your high ways shall be desolate. readings.label: His sentence
readings.original: It frequently happens that, to make the parts of a kingdom hold the better analogy with one another, and for the more convenience of expressing their mutual respects and actions, and sometimes of considering two or more kingdoms at once, the Prophets extend some part of the universe to the whole kingdom.
readings.modern: Often, so the parts of a kingdom will match each other, or so he can speak of two kingdoms at once, a prophet takes one piece of the universe and stretches it over the whole kingdom. Then you change the interpretation to match.

readings.label: Later wording in the same section
readings.original: But it happens sometimes that for the more convenience of describing any subject, the proportions are changed, and then the interpretation must be changed accordingly. Thus although a tree originally signifies an inferior great man, yet if it be represented large beyond proportion, so as to reach to the ends of the earth, it must signify a king whose dominions are proportionally great. So although a mountain originally signifies only a city, yet if it be so great as to fill the whole earth, it must by analogy signify the kingdoms of the earth subject to that city. And although wild beasts originally signify armies, yet if those armies by preying upon their neighbours at length grow into a kingdom, that kingdom may from its original be called a beast, especially if it continue to be supported by armies, and the beast be described great and powerful.
readings.modern: He says the same thing again, more fully, later in the definitions. When the scale is changed, the meaning changes with it. A tree that reaches the ends of the earth is no longer a great man under a king. It is a king whose dominion is that large. A mountain that fills the earth is no longer one city. It is the kingdoms subject to that city. A wild beast that started as an army, and grew by preying on its neighbours into a kingdom, may be called a beast for that reason, above all if armies still hold it up and the beast is drawn great and powerful.

proof.original: 30 It is usually supposed that the vices of nations were the reason why in Daniel and the Revelations they are represented by Beasts, and this may be sometimes allowed for a secondary reason especially in the revelations, but I cannot think it the authentic reason becaus a beast may as well be taken in a good sense as in a bad one. For Christ is represented by a Lyon as wel as Nebuchadnezzar, and some of the 12 tribes are characterized by beasts in Iacob's blessing as well as the 4 Monarchies in Daniel's visions: And therefore I must rather derive this type from armies whereby kingdoms are usually founded and upheld. For since armies are wild Beasts by Fig: 13, it is thence very natural to put a Beast for any kingdom which was originated from armies and frequently imploys them like a ravenous Beast to prey upon its neighbours. And this the prophetique doctrine of Iacob may teach us who called Iudah a Lyon from his getting the prey and being Prince of the Tribes; Issachar an Ass from his being in slavery, Dan a serpent from his laying stratagems and Benjamin a wolf from ravening and devouring the prey. And so descriptions of the beasts in Daniel almost wholly respect their politic constitution and pugnaciousnes excepting what is said of the little horn. And in the Revelation although the two-hornd Beast be not represented pugnatious, yet its merchants (chap 18) supply the place of armies since they prey upon the Kings of the earth by their sophistical merchandise no less then the other by force.

proof.original: this difference that when there is only an occasional mention of eyes as common and natural to animals (as for instance of the Goats Eyes Dan. 8.5, 21) they signify only that policy and counsel which is naturally to be met with in all kingdoms. But when their description is emphatical and not according to the course of natur they signify a Seer in the extraordinary and supernatural sense. Thus the Lambs seven eyes are called the seven spirits of God sent forth into all the earth. Apoc. 5.6. Which spirits in the beginning of the Apocalyps are in liew of the holy Ghost joyned with the Father and the Son; and Grace wished from them together with the Father and Son to signify that the Holy Ghost or prophetick Spirit is denoted by them. Whence some ancients have called the holy spirit, spiritum septemplicem. According to which way of speaking the seven eyes will signify the sevenfold prophetick spirit of the Lamb, by which as it were with a prophetick energy and lights he beholds and overlooks all the earth. As is again in Zech. 4.10 where these spirits are called the eyes of the Lord which run to and fro through the whole earth: an expression alluding to a mans eyes rolling to and fro. Again where the four Beasts are said to be full of eyes before and behind and their wings to be full of eyes within, this denotes them to signify prophetic multitudes. For as Beasts they signify multitudes and this the rather because of their many eyes,. Now their eyes in their wings because not without but only within denote an internal faculty of seing that is, their intellect and this illuminated not barely by the light of nature but by the Spirit because they are not mere men but servants and worshippers of the living God Apoc 4.8, 9. And their eyes before and behind signify not a faculty of seing only things present round about. (for then why had they not eyes on both sides and all over as well as before and behind) but a faculty of seing things future and past, and this is the perfect character of a Prophet And accordingly Apoc 5.9,10 you have them with the Elders thus prophesying Thou hast slain and hast redeemed us to God by thy blood and c, and we shall reign on the earth: So the eyes of the little horn in Daniel cap 7 I conceive signifies that horn to be a Seer of an extraordinary supernatural kind: One whose eyes are not spirits of truth like the Lambs eyes but lying spirits: A fals prophet For did those eyes signify only policy and cunning the other horns would have eyes as well as this though it may be not so good ones: under these eyes it is to be conceived that the Beast hath other eyes suitable to nature to signify the policy of the kingdoms denoted by all the horns, that of the little horn as well as the rest. And therefore the eyes which the little horn has besides these, such as none of the other horns have, must signify a further faculty of seeing such as no horn has but this. It is not therefore a Politician only but a seer of a higher kind or to speak in the Iewish language, a prophet, though a fals one.

proof.original: 35. And as eyes signify the chief kind of seing which the body represented by the animal is capable of, so a mouth for speaking and speaking with it where the words spoken are not set down, signifies the highest kind of speaking, that is dictating of laws and those by civil authority if the thing speaking be a body politick, or by divine authority if a body prophetick or Theological. Thus besides the mouth of the 4th beast Dan 7th common to all the kingdom signified by the horns (Dan 7) the little horn has another mouth proper to himself to signify his having a legislative power of such a kind as none of the other horns have. And what that power was, is there described plainly. He had a mouth speaking very great things vers 20, even great words against the most high and [thereby] wore out the saints of the most high, and thought to change times and laws and they were given into his hand for a time vers 25. This he did by the power of his mouth, which must be a legislative one and that in matters of religion because times and laws were given into his hand to change them in opposition to God and the saints. So where the Image of the Beast Apoc 13 is said to speak and cause that as many as would not worship the Image should be killed; it must be by some law that they were killed, and the Image is not the officer that killed them but the author of their being killed, that is the lawmaker. It spake and caused them to be killed that would not worship it; that is, It spake with authority so as to cause them to be killed that would not obey its voice. Speaking and causing here are ἕν διὰ δυοιν. So again where the two horned Beast spake as the Dragon and the ten horned Beast had a mouth like the Lyon (the first of Daniels four Beasts signifying the kingdom of Babylon) and spake great things and blasphemies against God: we are to understand that these beasts (each according to his authority) made Idolatrous laws and constitutions such as the diabolical Dragon and Babylonian Lyon made before. And so by the prophesying of the two witnesses we are to understand their promulging and spreading the laws and word of God according to the utmost power they are able to speak with. For this their prophesying is opposed to the speaking or prophesying of the fals prophet, and so signifies here not foretelling future things by immediate revelation, but ‡ the preaching to the world the word of God according to the right interpretation and meaning of it and propagating it in Gods name with all the authority they are able; as on the other hand the fals Prophet propagates fals interpretations and other lies in the name of his God, pretending the authority of his God, as the true prophets do that of theirs; to make his sentences pass for law and gain to himself a law making power in matters of religion.

proof.original: 37. The feet very fitly represent armies. For as they are the most active members, and the lowest parts of the Beast, and serve to support him, and to move upon, and to fight with: so Armies are much in motion, and the lowest of the people, and by them kingdoms are supported and carried to and fro, and they are the members wherewith kingdoms fight. This interpretation is also evident by the visions of Daniel: for the ten hornd Beast, to signify the use and power of his feet in fighting is represented with nails of brass and said to stamp with his feet what he devoured not with his teeth: which is as much as to say, that those neighbouring nations which were not devoured by perfect conquest and incorporated into the dition of this Empire, were yet, awed and bruised with its armies. That Idols may be called men is according to the common way of speaking: for they are images of men, and as we are wont to call the image of a Beast a Beast and the image of a bird a bird so we call the image of a man a man. And as this is the common way of speaking so it is the language of the scriptures. Thou hast played the harlot with many lovers yet return to me saith the Lord – she defiled the Land and committed adultery with stones and with stocks. Ier: 3.1, 9. I will destroy her vines and her figtrees whereof she said, These are my rewards that my lovers have given me — and I will visit upon her the days of Baalim wherein she – went after her lovers and forgot me saith the Lord. Hos: 2.12. Thou pouredst out thy fornications on every one that passed by — thou madest thy self Images of men and didst commit whoredom with them — thou hast committed fornication with the Egyptians great of flesh — thy filthines was poured out and thy nakedness discovered through thy whoredoms with thy lovers even with all the Idols of thy abominations Ezek. 16.15, 17, 26, 37. Aholah – doted on her lovers, on the Assyrians her neighbours which were clothed with blew, Capitains and Rulers all of them desirable young men, horsmen riding upon horses. Thus she committed her whoredoms with them, with all them that were chosen men of Assyria and with all on whome she doted, [even] with all their Idols Ezek: 23.5. And when her sister Aholibah saw this — she doted upon the Assyrians her neighbours Capitains and rulers clothed most gorgeously, horsmen riding upon horses, all of them desirable young men — and she increased her whoredoms, for when she saw men pourtrayed upon the wall, the Images of the Chaldeans pourtrayed with Vermilion girded with girdles upon their loins, exceeding in died attire upon their heads, all of them Princes to look to, after the manner of the Babylonians, she doted upon them and sent messengers unto them into Chaldea, and the Babylonians came to her into the bed of love, i.e. when she saw their Idols she doted upon them and sent for others to be made in their likeness and set up in her own land. vers 11.

readings.original: The throwing down of idols is represented by the falling of the stars, as a fig falleth from a fig tree.

proof.original: 65 The falling of the stars and departure of the heavens according to the precedent interpretation of stars and Heaven will signify the fall of great men and the departure of the glory of a Kingdom. And becaus Idols are sometimes considered as men by Def 63 therefore this emblem may be applyed either to a Kingdom of Idols or to a Kingdom of men, as the circumstances shall require. Thus Saint Stephen calls the Idol of Rempham a Star, saying: Ye took up the Tabernacle of Moloch and the Star of your God Rempham figures which ye made to worship them. Acts 7.43. It is indeed less usuall to represent Idols by the stars but it is more proper, becaus they being the Images of supposed celestial Gods, were thence in scripture called Gods and the host of heaven: and the analogy between the Vnivers and a kingdom will be more perfect when things which relate to heaven are represented by the heavenly bodies, and the parts of a Kingdom which respect the earth by things on the Earth then when they are confounded together: Yea this the scripture seems to insinuate when it calls Idols as well as stars the host of heaven And therefore we need not doubt to interpret stars of Idols and Heaven of their honour and dignity or rather of the orbicular roofs of their Temples, whenever that interpretation will best agree with the circumstances. And thus it happens in this definition. For here the allusions to the falling of Figs from a fig-tree and to the rolling of a scroll together, do by striking the imagination with an Idea of local motion make it a more lively representation of the ruining of a Kingdom of Idol-Gods then of a Kingdom of men. For the stars falling unto the earth as figs fall from a fig tree do most lively represent falling Idols, and Heaven departing as a Scroll when it is rolled together, the roof of a Temple gradually taken off, or cleaving asunder at its being thrown down.

It is indeed less usuall to represent Idols by the stars but it is more proper, because they being the Images of supposed celestial Gods, were thence in scripture called Gods and the host of heaven: and the analogy between the Universe and a kingdom will be more perfect when things which relate to heaven are represented by the heavenly bodies, and the parts of a Kingdom which respect the earth by things on the Earth then when they are confounded together: Yea this the scripture seems to insinuate when it calls Idols as well as stars the host of heaven And therefore we need not doubt to interpret stars of Idols and Heaven of their honour and dignity or rather of the orbicular roofs of their Temples, whenever that interpretation will best agree with the circumstances. And thus it happens in this definition. For here the allusions to the falling of Figs from a fig-tree and to the rolling of a scroll together, do by striking the imagination with an Idea of local motion make it a more lively representation of the ruining of a Kingdom of Idol-Gods then of a Kingdom of men. For the stars falling unto the earth as figs fall from a fig tree do most lively represent falling Idols, and Heaven departing as a Scroll when it is rolled together, the roof of a Temple gradually taken off, or cleaving asunder at its being thrown down.

proof.original: 44. Yet the celestial bodies are not to be interpreted so strictly of the persons of Kings and Princes but that the Sun and Moon may sometimes be used to signify in general the splendor and glory of a kingdom in as much as the Sun is the glory of the world by day and the moon by night: for thus the Chalde Paraphrast interprets them in Ier. 15.9, and Isa. 60.20. And so where the woman is said to be clothed with the sun and the moon under her feet, Rev. 12, the Sun and moon signify the glory of the righteousnes of Christ wherewith the Church is to be clothed, and of her own righteousnes which she is to put off but yet be supported by it as it borrows splendor from that sun and shines as it were by reflexion. And so where the Sun is turned into blackness and the moon into blood Ioel 2.31, and Rev. 6.12, I had rather understand it in general of the splendor of the Kingdom put out and the glory turned into bloodshed then interpret it only of the King and the next in dignity: for the perishing of those two persons infers not the overthrow of the Kingdom; whereas in Ioel the turning of the Sun into darknes and the moon into blood is made the description of that universal overthrow of the gentile Kingdoms and mighty slaughter of all their armies which is to happen at the great day of God Almighty, as is at large described in the next chapter.
